iOS 27.2 is coming sooner than you might expect. iOS 27.1 will only bring changes to the iPhone Duo, so other users will have to wait for iOS 27.2 for new features. Here's when the update is expected to roll out.

iOS 27.2 is confirmed to launch in October, expected later this month.

Apple is currently testing iOS 27.2 beta, which has been underway for several weeks. This is notably earlier than the typical testing timeline for an x.2 release, and there is a good reason for it.

The iPhone Duo is set to launch on October 23 with iOS 27.1 pre-installed. All signs point to other iPhone models skipping that update entirely and jumping straight to iOS 27.2.

By keeping iOS 27.1 exclusive to the iPhone Duo, Apple can avoid revealing more about the software experience during the beta testing process. This is why iOS 27.2 has entered beta testing earlier.

When is iOS 27.2 launching? We know it's coming in October.

When iOS 27 first debuted last month, Apple said Siri AI would gain support for French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish "next month."

Those new Siri languages are included in iOS 27.2, further confirming an October rollout. Additional features in iOS 27.2 include:

  • User profiles in the Apple TV app
  • Dual Capture in Group FaceTime
  • New Suggestions feature in Messages
  • Major redesign of the Up Next interface in Apple Podcasts
  • Design refresh for Apple Books

Following tradition, Apple typically rolls out the first feature update to its new OS version at the end of October, and this year should be no different. The week of October 26 looks to be the most likely timeframe.

iOS 27.2 could also arrive a little earlier, especially if the new hardware launching next week ships with this version pre-installed. However, the rumored Home lineup is not expected to go on sale immediately, with shipments expected to begin in the final week of October — right alongside iOS 27.2, tvOS 27.2, and HomePod 27.2.
